newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Occidental sees work restarting soon in Cano Limon.
newsitem.headline: Occidental sees work restarting soon in Cano Limon.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp said it could restart operations at its Cano Limon oil field in eastern Colombia "within 48 hours or less" following news that repair work had begun on the crippled Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline, a company spokesman said.
He declined, however, to speculate whether the resumption of operations would mean the force majeure declared in the field earlier this week could be lifted immediately.
"Conceivably (operations can restart) within 48 hours or less if we don't have any more attacks against the pipeline," an Occidental spokesman said.

The comments came minutes after technicians of the state oil company Ecopetrol began repair work on the pipeline near the town of Arauquita in Arauca province -- the site where national Liberation Army (ELN) rebels blew it up on July 10 in the secoind dynamite attack in four days.
The spokesman said that as soon as pipeline repairs were completed Occidental would begin pumping out crude stored on-site at the Cano Limon field.
He said it would take "about a day" to evacuate the storage site after which production proper would restart.

Occidental cut daily production from about 175,000 barrels per day to 70,000 barrels per day after the first of the two pipeline bombings on July 6. It then shut in the field on July 10 after the second attack.

On Tuesday this week the U.S. multinational declared force majeure in the field, the first time ever since it came on stream, announcing it was temporarily laying off as many as 200 contract workers and company employees.
